name: @tigerhill/mcp-tools

tools.name: th_run
tools.description:
Execute a Playwright test script and return results with evidence.

This tool runs a Playwright test in a subprocess and captures:
- Test pass/fail status
- Failed step information (if any)
- Error messages and classification
- Screenshots and DOM snapshots for failures
- Execution duration

Use this tool to:
1. Run individual test scripts
2. Verify test repairs work correctly
3. Collect failure evidence for diagnosis

script_path.description: Path to the Playwright test script (.spec.ts file)

headed.description: Run browser in headed mode (visible window). Default: true

workspace.description: Test workspace directory. Defaults to TH_WORKSPACE env var (auto-set when running in workspace).

storageState.description: Path to storage state JSON file for authenticated sessions (e.g., "profiles/admin.json")

project.description: Playwright project name (browser) to run, e.g. "chromium", "webkit", "firefox"

tools.name: th_run_batch
tools.description:
Run multiple Playwright test scripts matching a pattern or directory.

This tool runs multiple tests and returns aggregated results. Use it to:
1. Run all tests in a directory: "scripts/ui/auth/"
2. Run tests matching a glob pattern: "scripts/**/*.spec.ts"
3. Verify a feature after code changes

Returns:
- Summary: total/passed/failed counts
- Per-file results with status and error details
- Total execution time

Example patterns:
- "scripts/ui/auth/" - All tests in the auth directory
- "scripts/**/*.spec.ts" - All spec files recursively
- "scripts/ui/**/*login*.spec.ts" - Login-related tests

pattern.description: Glob pattern or directory path (e.g., "scripts/ui/auth/" or "scripts/**/*.spec.ts")

headed.description: Run browser in headed mode. Default: true

timeout.description: Test timeout in milliseconds per file. Default: 60000

workspace.description: Test workspace directory. Defaults to TH_WORKSPACE env var (auto-set when running in workspace).

storageState.description: Path to storage state JSON file for authenticated sessions (e.g., "profiles/admin.json")

role.description: Role name for multi-role testing (e.g., "admin", "operator"). Used with storageState.

project.description: Playwright project name (browser) to run, e.g. "chromium", "webkit", "firefox"

env.description: Environment name (staging, production, dev). Loads env/<name>.env.yaml. Default: staging

workers.description: Number of parallel Playwright workers (positive integer >= 1). Default: project config (usually 1)

retries.description: Number of retries for failed tests (non-negative integer >= 0). Default: project config

shard.description: Shard tests for CI distribution in "i/n" format (e.g. "1/2"). 1<=i<=n

tools.name: th_generate_script
tools.description:
Generate a Playwright test script from a Case YAML file.

This tool reads a Case file (YAML format) and generates a Playwright TypeScript test script.

**Case YAML format**:
```yaml
id: TC_LOGIN_001
title: 用户登录成功
specId: SPEC_LOGIN_001
kind: ui
priority: P0
steps:
  - tag: NAVIGATE
    action: goto
    target: /login
    intent: 进入登录页面
  - tag: INPUT_USERNAME
    action: fill
    target: input[name="username"]
    value: "testuser"
    intent: 输入用户名
checkpoints:
  - tag: CP_LOGIN_SUCCESS
    expect: 登录后跳转到首页
```

**Generated script**:
- Uses Playwright test() structure
- Preserves Step TAGs as comments
- Includes intent comments for repair context
- Adds TODO markers for checkpoints

**Usage**:
1. Generate script from single case: th_generate_script({case_file: "cases/ui/auth/TC_LOGIN_001.case.yaml"})
2. Specify output: th_generate_script({case_file: "...", output_path: "scripts/custom/"})
3. Override base URL: th_generate_script({case_file: "...", base_url: "http://staging.example.com"})

case_file.description: Path to the Case YAML file

base_url.description: Base URL for the application. Auto-detected from playwright.config.ts if not specified

output_path.description: Output directory or file path. Auto-derived from case path if not specified

strict.description: Strict validation mode. If true (default), rejects Cases with missing required fields like afterStep, assertionType. Set to false to allow incomplete Cases with TODO placeholders.

workspace.description: Test workspace directory. Defaults to TH_WORKSPACE env var (auto-set when running in workspace).

locale.description: Locale for Navigator altLocators selection (e.g., "zh-CN", "en-US"). When specified, prefers altLocators[locale] over default locator.

tools.name: th_case_validate
tools.description:
Validate Case YAML files for completeness and correctness.

This tool checks Case files against the required schema and returns validation results.

**Validation checks**:
- Required fields: id, title, steps, checkpoints
- Step fields: number, tag, action, intent, targetElement
- Checkpoint fields: id (not tag!), description (not expect!), afterStep, assertionType, locator
- Field naming: navigate vs goto, targetElement vs target
- Login preconditions: warns if navigating to auth-required paths without preconditions

**Strict mode** (default: true):
- Treats missing afterStep, assertionType as errors
- Requires all checkpoints to have locator for visibility/text assertions
- Blocks script generation for invalid Cases

**Use this tool**:
1. After generating Cases to verify correctness
2. Before calling th_generate_script to catch errors early
3. To batch validate all Cases in a directory

**Returns**: { valid: boolean, errors: [...], warnings: [...] }

case_file.description: Path to a single Case YAML file, or glob pattern (e.g., "cases/**/*.case.yaml")

strict.description: Strict mode: treat missing afterStep/assertionType as errors. Default: true

workspace.description: Test workspace directory. Defaults to TH_WORKSPACE env var (auto-set when running in workspace).

tools.name: th_candidates
tools.description:
Generate locator candidates for a failed element based on DOM snapshot.

This tool analyzes a DOM snapshot and generates alternative locators using a 7-level priority strategy:
1. **data-testid** (95% confidence) - Most stable, recommended
2. **role + name** (90% confidence) - Semantic, accessible
3. **label** (85% confidence) - For form elements
4. **placeholder** (80% confidence) - For inputs
5. **text** (75% confidence) - Content-based
6. **css** (60% confidence) - Structure-based
7. **xpath** (50% confidence) - Fallback

Returns up to 5 candidates sorted by confidence. Use th_repair to apply the selected candidate.

dom.description: DOM snapshot (HTML string) from the failed test evidence

failed_selector.description: The original selector that failed to find the element

target_description.description: Description of the target element (from script comments like "// 目标元素：登录按钮")

tools.name: th_classify
tools.description:
Classify the type of test failure to determine the appropriate repair strategy.

Failure classes:
- **LocatorDrift**: Element exists but locator method is outdated → auto_repair
- **MinorUIChange**: Minor UI text changes → auto_repair
- **FlowDrift**: Business flow changed → human_review
- **Transient**: Network/timing issues → retry
- **Harness**: Script/config problems → human_review
- **UIBlocked**: Modals/overlays blocking → auto_repair

urlTrace.description: URL navigation trace in chronological order (optional, from th_run result)

business_impact.description: Business impact level from Case YAML (optional, for failure priority sorting)

tools.name: th_verify
tools.description:
Verify a repair proposal against the Repair Envelope rules.

The Repair Envelope defines what changes are allowed during automatic repairs:
✅ Allowed: Change locator strategy, adjust wait times (with limits), add scroll
❌ Forbidden: Modify Step TAGs, Checkpoints, assertions, or skip steps

Use this tool before applying any repair to ensure it's within bounds.

diff.description: Unified diff of the proposed change

tools.name: th_envelope
tools.description: Get the Repair Envelope rules that constrain automatic repairs.

tools.name: th_repair
tools.description:
Apply a repair diff to a test script file.

This tool applies a unified diff to fix a broken locator or other allowed changes.
Before applying, it validates the repair against the Repair Envelope rules.

**Process**:
1. Validates the diff against Repair Envelope constraints
2. Creates a backup of the original file
3. Applies the diff to the script
4. Returns success status and backup path

**Repair Envelope enforced**:
- ✅ Allowed: Locator changes, wait time adjustments (+10s max), scroll additions
- ❌ Forbidden: Step TAG changes, Checkpoint changes, assertion weakening

Use th_verify first to check if the repair is valid before applying.

file_path.description: Path to the test script file to repair

diff.description: Unified diff format string with the repair changes

dry_run.description: If true, validate only without applying. Default: false

tools.name: th_eval
tools.description:
Evaluate an AI-generated web application for quality and compliance.

This tool opens a URL, captures evidence (screenshot, console logs, accessibility tree),
and returns structured evaluation results. The evaluation covers:

**Dimensions**:
- Deploy: Page load status and response time
- Health: JavaScript errors, network failures, console warnings
- Structure: Element detection, accessibility analysis

**Evidence Collected**:
- Full-page screenshot
- HTML snapshot
- Accessibility tree (JSON)
- Console logs (errors, warnings, info)

**Scoring**:
- Overall score (0-100) based on health (60%) and structure (40%)
- Health score: -15 per JS error, -10 per network error
- Structure score: +5 per element type found (max 50), -10 per accessibility issue

**Usage**:
After calling th_eval, analyze the user_prompt against the collected evidence
to assess whether the generated app meets the user's requirements.

app_url.description: URL of the application to evaluate

iframe_selector.description: CSS selector for preview iframe. Default: "#preview-iframe"

user_prompt.description: Original user instruction for compliance evaluation

tools.name: th_semantic_filter
tools.description:
Filter locator candidates based on semantic similarity to the original intent.

This tool applies a two-layer filtering process:
1. **Coarse filter** (rule-based): Checks role compatibility and keyword overlap
2. **AI filter** (optional): Uses AI to assess semantic match when configured

**Use cases**:
- Filter out candidates that don't match the original element type (e.g., link vs button)
- Remove candidates whose text content is unrelated to the target description
- Reduce false positives before attempting repairs

**Returns**: Filtered candidates list and reasons for exclusions.

candidates.description: Array of LocatorCandidate objects from th_candidates

target_description.description: Description of the target element intent

api_key.description: Gemini API key for AI filtering (optional)

tools.name: th_ai_candidates
tools.description:
Generate locator candidates using AI analysis of the DOM.

Use this tool when rule-based candidates fail or need smarter alternatives.
The AI analyzes the DOM snapshot and generates Playwright locators based on:
- Element semantics and purpose
- Accessibility attributes
- Visual hierarchy
- User intent from description

**Best practices**:
1. First try th_candidates for rule-based candidates
2. If all fail semantic filtering, use this tool
3. Provide failed candidates to avoid duplicates

**Returns**: AI-generated candidates with confidence scores and reasoning.

target_description.description: Description of what element you are trying to find

dom_snapshot.description: HTML DOM snapshot of the page

error_message.description: The error message from the failed test (optional)

tools.name: th_repair_full
tools.description:
Run a complete test repair pipeline: test → classify → candidates → filter → apply → verify.

This is the recommended tool for one-click test repair. It handles:
1. Running the test and capturing failure evidence
2. Classifying the failure type
3. Generating candidate locators
4. Applying semantic filtering
5. Trying candidates one by one
6. Verifying the repair works
7. Rolling back if verification fails

**Supports**:
- Rule-based candidates with 7-strategy priority
- AI-enhanced repair when rules fail (if api_key provided)
- Automatic rollback on verification failure
- Detailed repair reports

**Returns**: Repair result with success status, applied changes, and report.

script_path.description: Path to the test script file

dry_run.description: If true, show repair plan without applying. Default: false

headed.description: Run browser in headed mode. Default: true

api_key.description: Gemini API key for AI-enhanced repair (optional)

workspace.description: Test workspace directory. Defaults to TH_WORKSPACE env var (auto-set when running in workspace).

storageState.description: Path to storage state JSON file for authenticated sessions (e.g., "profiles/admin.json")

role.description: Role name for multi-role testing (e.g., "admin", "operator"). Used with storageState.

chain_mode.description: Enable multi-step chain repair. When a repair succeeds but re-running reveals a NEW failure at a DIFFERENT step, automatically continues to the next round (max 3 rounds). Default: false

max_chain_rounds.description: Maximum repair rounds in chain mode. Default: 3

tools.name: th_find_affected_tests
tools.description:
Find affected test scripts based on changed source files.

This tool maps code changes to test scripts using a multi-layer strategy:
1. **Case relatedFiles** (HIGH confidence) - Explicit mapping in Case YAML
2. **Directory mapping rules** (MEDIUM confidence) - Pattern-based mapping from .tigerhill.json
3. **Tag matching** (LOW confidence) - Feature-based tag matching as fallback

**Use this tool to**:
- Determine which tests to run after code changes
- Support CI/CD pipelines with targeted test execution
- Help developers understand test coverage for their changes

**Returns**: List of affected test scripts with confidence levels and reasons.

changed_files.description: List of changed source file paths (relative to project root)

mode.description: Mode: "precise" returns only high-confidence matches, "safe" includes fallback suggestions. Default: safe

root_dir.description: Project root directory. Default: current working directory

tools.name: th_ui_blocker
tools.description:
Detect and generate code to handle UI blockers (modals, overlays, cookie banners).

Use this when tests fail with "element is obscured" or "intercepts pointer events" errors.

**Generates**:
- Escape key press attempt
- Click handlers for common close button patterns
- Support for custom selectors

**Returns**: Playwright code snippet to inject before the failing step.

error_message.description: Error message to check if it is a UI blocker issue

custom_selectors.description: Custom close button selectors for your app

tools.name: th_nav_update
tools.description:
Update the Navigator site map with page and element information.

This tool updates the Navigator YAML file (navigator/ui/site-map.yaml) which stores:
- Page definitions (id, path, title, elements)
- Element locators discovered during exploration
- Page navigation relationships

**Actions**:
- add_page: Add or update a page with elements
- add_element: Add element to existing page
- update_element: Update element locator and/or altLocators (supports altLocators-only update)
- update_page: Update page info
- remove_page: Remove a page
- remove_element: Remove element from page

**⚠️ CRITICAL: Required Elements for Each Page**:
When exploring a page, you MUST collect ALL of these element types if they exist:
1. **表格 (table)**: 数据列表、产品表格、用户列表等
2. **筛选器 (select/input)**: 下拉筛选、搜索框、日期范围选择器
3. **模态框 (dialog)**: 新增弹窗、编辑弹窗、确认对话框
4. **按钮 (button)**: 新增、编辑、删除、保存、取消等操作按钮
5. **表单元素 (input/textarea/select)**: 输入框、文本域、下拉选择

**Failure to collect these elements will cause script generation to produce TODO placeholders instead of valid code!**

**Workflow**:
1. Use Playwright MCP to explore a page
2. **Identify ALL key elements** (tables, filters, modals, buttons, forms)
3. Call th_nav_update to record findings
4. Verify no critical elements are missing before proceeding

**Example** (complete page with required elements):
```json
{
  "action": "add_page",
  "page": {
    "id": "products",
    "path": "/products",
    "title": "产品列表",
    "elements": [
      { "name": "产品列表表格", "locator": "table.product-table", "type": "table" },
      { "name": "类型筛选器", "locator": "select[name='category']", "type": "select" },
      { "name": "搜索框", "locator": "input[placeholder='搜索']", "type": "input" },
      { "name": "新增产品按钮", "locator": "button:has-text('新增')", "type": "button" },
      { "name": "新增产品模态框", "locator": ".modal.add-product", "type": "dialog" },
      { "name": "新增_名称输入框", "locator": ".modal input[name='name']", "type": "input" },
      { "name": "新增_保存按钮", "locator": ".modal button:has-text('保存')", "type": "button" }
    ]
  }
}
```

**Integration with Cases**:
- Locators in Navigator can be referenced by Cases
- Use `th nav validate` to check Case locators against Navigator
- Missing elements will cause validateCaseStrict() to emit warnings

options.description: Available options for select/combobox elements (click to expand and capture all options)

sampleValues.description: Sample valid values for input fields

source.description: API endpoint or data source description

visibleTo.description: Role IDs that can see this element (e.g., ["admin"]). Omit for elements visible to all roles.

enabledFor.description: Role IDs that can interact with this element (e.g., ["admin"]). Omit for elements enabled for all roles.

navigatesTo.description: Page IDs this page can navigate to

trigger.description: Element name that triggers this transition

transitions.description: Page transitions with trigger details (coexists with navigatesTo)

visibleTo.description: Role IDs that can access this page (e.g., ["admin", "editor"]). Omit for pages visible to all roles.

element.description: Element to add or update (for add_element/update_element). Include options/sampleValues/dynamicData for hidden data.

altLocators.description: Alternative locators for anti-drift (e.g., {"testid": "[data-testid='btn']", "secondary": "role/name locator"}). For update_element, locator and altLocators are both optional but at least one is required.

sampleValues.description: Sample valid values for input fields

externalJump.description: External site jump info (OAuth etc). Record even if cannot automate.

visibleTo.description: Role IDs that can see this element (e.g., ["admin"]). Omit for elements visible to all roles.

enabledFor.description: Role IDs that can interact with this element (e.g., ["admin"]). Omit for elements enabled for all roles.

navigatorPath.description: Custom Navigator file path. Default: navigator/ui/site-map.yaml

projectName.description: Project name (used when creating new Navigator)

baseUrl.description: Base URL (used when creating new Navigator)

tools.name: th_nav_check
tools.description:
Check Navigator (site-map.yaml) for completeness and quality issues.

**Use this tool after exploring to verify the Navigator is ready for Case/Script generation.**

**Checks performed**:
- baseUrl: Must be set (not placeholder like example.com)
- description: Every page should have a description
- elements: Every page should have elements
- sampleValues: Input elements should have sample values
- options: Select elements should have options
- visibleTo: Role-specific pages should have visibleTo
- navigatesTo: Pages with nav links should define navigatesTo (critical for SPAs without URL routing)
- pathCollapse: Warns if all pages have path="/" (valid only for pure state-driven SPAs)

**Returns**: { valid: boolean, errors: [...], warnings: [...], infos: [...] }

**When to use**:
1. After completing exploration of all pages
2. Before generating Spec/Case files
3. After multi-role exploration to verify role attributes

strict.description: Strict mode: also check element-level visibleTo for multi-role projects. Default: false

workspace.description: Test workspace directory. Defaults to TH_WORKSPACE env var (auto-set when running in workspace).

tools.name: th_nav_depth_check
tools.description:
Compare actual page DOM element census against Navigator recordings to check exploration depth.

**Use this tool** after recording a page to verify sufficient element coverage.

**Input**:
- pageId: which page to check
- domCensus: actual element counts from browser_run_code census script
- threshold: coverage threshold (0-100, default 80)

**Output**:
- coverage: 0-100 weighted ratio
- gaps: specific missing element categories with counts and IDs
- suggestions: actionable next steps
- sufficient: whether coverage meets threshold

**Workflow**:
1. Run census script via browser_run_code on the current page
2. Call th_nav_depth_check with the census data
3. If !sufficient: follow suggestions to record missing elements
4. Repeat until sufficient or max 2 iterations

pageId.description: Page ID in Navigator to check

domCensus.description: DOM element census data from browser_run_code

workspace.description: Test workspace directory. Defaults to TH_WORKSPACE env var or cwd.

tools.name: th_ai_verify
tools.description:
AI-assisted page verification for visual and semantic checks.

⚠️ IMPORTANT: This is a SUPPLEMENTARY verification, NOT a replacement for Playwright assertions.
Use hard assertions for critical business logic (login success, URL changes, element states).

**When to use AI verification**:
- Visual/layout checks: "page layout looks correct", "no visual glitches"
- Semantic checks: "welcome message contains username", "no error messages visible"
- Exploratory validation: additional review after tests pass

**When NOT to use**:
- Critical business logic (use hard assertions instead)
- Anything that can be precisely verified with locators/URLs/text

**Returns**: { pass: boolean, reason: string, confidence: number, findings: [...] }

screenshot.description: Base64 encoded screenshot of the page

dom.description: HTML DOM snapshot of the page (optional, enhances analysis)

expected.description: Array of expected conditions to verify (e.g., ["页面显示用户头像", "没有错误提示"])

api_key.description: Gemini API key (optional, falls back to GEMINI_API_KEY env)

tools.name: th_evidence_review
tools.description:
AI-powered evidence review for test results.

Analyzes screenshots and DOM snapshots to detect issues that Playwright assertions might miss:
- Page still showing loading spinner
- Error messages or alerts visible
- Layout issues or broken elements
- Console errors in the page

**When to use**:
1. After a test passes but you want to verify visual correctness
2. When investigating a test that passed but the feature seems broken
3. For additional confidence beyond deterministic assertions

**Input options**:
- evidence_dir: Path to evidence directory (contains screenshots, DOM snapshots)
- OR provide individual fields: screenshot_path, dom_snapshot, console_logs

**Returns**: { passed, confidence, findings[] }

screenshot_path.description: Path to screenshot file (alternative to evidence_dir)

expected_results.description: List of expected results to verify

api_key.description: Gemini API key (optional, falls back to .tigerhill.local.json or env)

tools.name: th_load_case
tools.description:
Load and validate a Case YAML file for live execution.

**Returns**: Case data with validation results (errors, warnings).

**Use this tool** as the first step in live execution to load the Case
that will be executed step by step via Playwright MCP.

If validation.valid is false, do NOT proceed with execution.

workspace.description: Test workspace directory. Defaults to TH_WORKSPACE env var (auto-set when running in workspace).

tools.name: th_nav_query
tools.description:
Look up an element's Playwright locator from the Navigator (site-map.yaml).

**Use this tool** during live execution to resolve each step's targetElement
to an actual locator before calling Playwright MCP actions.

Returns the locator string if found, or null with available elements for disambiguation.

page_id.description: Optional page ID for disambiguation when same element name exists across pages

workspace.description: Test workspace directory. Defaults to TH_WORKSPACE env var (auto-set when running in workspace).

tools.name: th_init_execution_record
tools.description:
Initialize a new execution recording session for live Case execution.

**Use this tool** after loading the Case and before executing steps.
Returns an execution_id that must be passed to all subsequent recording calls.

viewport.description: Browser viewport size. Default: { width: 1280, height: 720 }

tools.name: th_record_step
tools.description:
Record the result of a single step execution during live mode.

**Use this tool** after each Playwright MCP action completes (or fails)
to build the execution record incrementally.

verified_locator.description: The locator that was actually used and verified working

data.description: Action data (fill value, navigate URL, etc.)

status.description: Step execution status: executed (default) | skipped (when stateGuard condition already satisfied)

reason.description: Skip reason when status=skipped (e.g. "stateGuard:authenticated already satisfied")

tools.name: th_record_checkpoint
tools.description:
Record the result of a checkpoint verification during live execution.

**Use this tool** after verifying each checkpoint (via browser_snapshot, browser_evaluate, etc.)
to record whether the assertion passed or failed.

after_step.description: The step number this checkpoint follows

expected_value.description: The expected value from Case checkpoint

tools.name: th_finalize_execution
tools.description:
Finalize the execution record after all steps and checkpoints are processed.

**Use this tool** as the last step in live execution to mark the record complete
and generate a summary.

Status rules:
- completed: all steps passed AND all checkpoints passed
- partial: some steps/checkpoints failed but execution continued
- failed: execution was aborted

tools.name: th_report
tools.description:
Generate a suite report from batch run results.

Reads the latest batch results and generates a summary report with:
- Pass/fail counts and pass rate
- Per-test results with error details
- Comparison with previous run (new failures, fixed tests, pass rate delta)

Reports are saved to .th-output/reports/ for historical tracking.

evidence_path.description: Path to the batch evidence directory containing results.json

workspace.description: Test workspace directory. Defaults to TH_WORKSPACE env var.

format.description: Output format. "json" returns structured report object, "markdown" returns formatted markdown string for PR comments/Issue bodies. Defaults to "json".

tools.name: th_history
tools.description:
Query test run history and detect flaky tests.

Reads .th-output/history.jsonl and calculates flakiness scores.
- Flakiness score 0 = stable (always pass or always fail)
- Flakiness score 100 = maximally unstable (50/50 pass/fail)

Use after th_run_batch to record results, or to query historical trends.
Use action "failure_patterns" to see failure class distribution and recurring patterns.

action.description: Action: record (save batch results), query (list history), flaky (show flaky tests), failure_patterns (show failure class distribution)

evidence_path.description: Path to batch evidence directory (for record action)

last_n.description: Number of recent runs to analyze (default: 10)

tools.name: th_memory
tools.description:
Manage project-level memory — accumulated domain knowledge across test runs.

Memory stores failure patterns, repair insights, fragile areas, and test strategies.
Storage: .th-output/project-memory.jsonl (append-only JSONL).

Actions:
- write: Append memory entries (manual or programmatic)
- query: Search memory by category/tags/keyword with limit
- learn: Auto-derive memory from test history (failure patterns + fragile areas)
- summary: Get a text summary of current memory state

action.description: Action: write (append entries), query (search), learn (auto-derive from history), summary (text overview)

entries.description: Memory entries to write (for write action)

tags.description: Filter by tags — any match (for query action)

keyword.description: Keyword search in content (for query action)

limit.description: Max results to return (for query action, default: 20)

workspace.description: Test workspace directory. Defaults to TH_WORKSPACE env var.

tools.name: th_security_check
tools.description:
Check HTTP security headers and cookie security for a URL.

Checks for:
- Critical: HSTS (Strict-Transport-Security)
- High: X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, CSP
- Medium: X-XSS-Protection, Referrer-Policy
- Low: Permissions-Policy, Cache-Control
- Cookie: Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite flags

Returns a security score (0-100) and detailed findings.

url.description: URL to check security headers for

check_cookies.description: Whether to check cookie security (default: true)

tools.name: th_perf_check
tools.description:
Collect and evaluate Core Web Vitals performance metrics for a URL.

Metrics collected:
- FCP (First Contentful Paint): good ≤1.8s, poor >3s
- LCP (Largest Contentful Paint): good ≤2.5s, poor >4s
- CLS (Cumulative Layout Shift): good ≤0.1, poor >0.25
- TTFB (Time to First Byte): good ≤800ms, poor >1.8s
- DOM Content Loaded, Page Load, resource count, transfer size

Returns a performance score (0-100), per-metric ratings, and raw data.
Uses Playwright to navigate and collect metrics via Performance API.

tools.name: th_quality_gate
tools.description:
Pre-submit quality gate for three-role collaboration (Ralph-Lisa-Tiger).

Scans test scripts for anti-patterns and checks report statistics consistency.

Anti-pattern rules (built-in):
- NO_ALWAYS_TRUE (critical): expect(true).toBe(true)
- NO_SILENT_PASS (critical): catch blocks that silently pass
- NO_CONSOLE_ASSERTION (critical): console.log used as assertion
- NO_EMPTY_CATCH (high): empty catch blocks
- NO_HARDCODED_WAIT (medium): waitForTimeout with long delays

Statistics consistency checks:
- total == passed + failed
- passRate matches passed/total
- detail results count matches summary

Returns: { passed, antiPatterns, statsConsistency, summary }

files.description: Test files to scan for anti-patterns. Each item needs path and content.

script_pattern.description: Glob pattern to find test scripts (e.g., "scripts/**/*.spec.ts"). Used when files not provided directly.

report_summary.description: Report summary to validate for consistency

Run a CLI command and verify its output.

Execute a shell command and check exit code, stdout, stderr.
Use for testing CLI tools, scripts, and command-line interfaces.

tools.name: th_a11y_check
tools.description:
Run accessibility (a11y) checks on a web page using axe-core.

Integrates axe-core via Playwright to detect WCAG violations. Returns structured results
with violation details, impact severity, and remediation guidance.

**WCAG Levels**:
- wcag2a: Level A (minimum)
- wcag2aa: Level AA (recommended, default)
- wcag2aaa: Level AAA (strictest)
- best-practice: AA + axe best practices

**Returns**:
- passed: true if zero violations
- violations: Array with ruleId, impact (critical/serious/moderate/minor), description, affected nodes
- summary: Count by impact level
- evidence_path: Directory with screenshot and full results JSON

**Usage**:
1. Basic check: th_a11y_check({ url: "http://localhost:3000" })
2. Strict check: th_a11y_check({ url: "...", level: "wcag2aaa" })
3. Scoped check: th_a11y_check({ url: "...", include: ["#main-content"] })

url.description: Target page URL to check for accessibility violations

include.description: CSS selectors to limit check scope (e.g., ["#main-content"])

exclude.description: CSS selectors to exclude from check (e.g., [".third-party-widget"])

workspace.description: Test workspace directory. Defaults to TH_WORKSPACE env var.

tools.description: Generate a JavaScript click script for use with browser_evaluate when browser_click fails (TH-005). Common on React/Vue/Angular apps where coordinate-based MCP clicks do not trigger synthetic event handlers. Returns a JS expression string that can be passed directly to browser_evaluate.

selector.description: CSS selector of the element to click (e.g., "[data-test=\"login-button\"]", "#submit", ".btn-primary")

tools.name: th_coverage
tools.description:
Generate a Spec→Case→Script coverage matrix (RTM).

Scans the project's specs/, cases/, scripts/ directories and cross-references
all three layers to produce a coverage report. Identifies:
- Uncovered Specs (no test cases written)
- Orphaned Cases (specId doesn't match any Spec file)
- Missing Scripts (Case exists but no script generated)

Options:
- priority: Filter by minimum case priority (P0/P1/P2) — only include cases at or above this level
- with_results: Merge latest test history (pass/fail) into each case entry

Returns summary stats, the full matrix, and prioritized suggestions for improving coverage.

workspace.description: Test workspace directory. Defaults to TH_WORKSPACE env var.

project_name.description: Project name for the report header. Defaults to workspace directory name.

format.description: Output format. "json" returns structured matrix, "markdown" returns formatted report. Defaults to "json".

priority.description: Filter by minimum case priority. P0 = only P0, P1 = P0+P1, P2 = all (default).

with_results.description: Merge latest test run results into coverage entries. Adds lastResult/lastDurationMs per case and passedCases/failedCases to summary.
